# Incident Report — Traffic Analysis Exercise, 2022-01-07

**Evidence:** `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,880 packets, single interface, no separate IDS export provided). Analyzed with tshark only, no internet lookups performed.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 192.168.1.216 | DHCP, all subsequent traffic |
| MAC address | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 | Ethernet source on every frame from the host |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** | DHCP option 12 (hostname), DNS/mDNS self-registration, Kerberos client name `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$` — all three agree. (Note: legacy NBNS broadcasts show "DESKTOP-GXNYNO2", a one-character variance in the older NetBIOS name service; the three independent, more authoritative sources above agree on GXMYNO2.) |
| Logged-in domain user | **steve.smith** | Kerberos AS/TGS exchanges with DC 192.168.1.2, realm SPOONWATCH.NET |
| AD domain / DC | SPOONWATCH.NET, DC = SPOONWATCH-DC (192.168.1.2) | DNS SRV records, LDAP/Kerberos traffic |

Capture starts 2022-01-07 20:04:09 (local, +0400). All traffic through roughly the first 3 minutes is normal DHCP/AD/domain-join chatter. Nothing in this pcap shows the initial delivery vector (no phishing email, exploit, or dropper download) — the malware is already resident and begins talking to its controller at 20:07:32.

## Malware family and attribution

**Behavioral attribution, not signature-confirmed.** No Suricata/IDS alert export was provided alongside the pcap, and this environment has no internet access to check file hashes against a reputation database, so nothing here is hash/YARA-confirmed. The behavior observed is consistent with a **RedLine Stealer**-style modular info-stealer/loader:

- All malicious traffic is a single sustained plaintext HTTP session (TCP stream 65, 20:07:32–20:07:40) to **2.56.57.108:80**, contacted directly by IP with no preceding DNS lookup.
- The HTTP client sends a non-browser, hardcoded fingerprint on every request: no `User-Agent`, `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`, `Accept-Charset: iso-8859-1, utf-8, utf-16, *;q=0.1`, `Accept: text/html, application/xml;q=0.9, application/xhtml+xml, image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/x-xbitmap, */*;q=0.1`.
- It fetches 7 payloads via `POST` to `/osk//1.jpg` … `/osk//7.jpg`, each a `multipart/form-data` "checkin" with a 25-byte empty body; the server responses (mislabeled `Content-Type: image/jpeg`) are actually Windows PE32 DLLs (verified by magic bytes `MZ`).
- It then `POST`s to `/osk//main.php` (empty response), then makes a final `POST /osk/` that **uploads** 379,629 bytes from the host to the server.
- That final upload's multipart body sets a non-standard `Content-Type: zip` and carries a file named `_5861695120.zip` (random-numeric filename) containing a stolen-data log with the folder/file layout: `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `system.txt`, `outlook.txt`, `pvk/`, `screenshot.jpg`.

This staged pattern — fake-jpg plugin DLLs pulled from a single IP-based gate, then a themed browser/credential/wallet-data archive exfiltrated back to the same gate — matches publicly documented RedLine Stealer log structure and C2 behavior. Treat the family name as a **behavioral best-fit assessment**, not a certainty.

## Indicators of compromise (all observed directly in this capture)

**C2 / exfiltration endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (HTTP, plaintext) — sole malicious endpoint in the capture. No domain name resolves to it; contacted by hardcoded IP.

**Malicious domains**
- None observed. All DNS/TLS SNI activity besides internal AD lookups resolves to legitimate Microsoft infrastructure (Windows Update, WNS, MSN, Bing, telemetry). The attacker infrastructure was reached by raw IP only.

**Malicious URLs (all to 2.56.57.108)**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` (POST, payload downloads)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` (POST)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (POST, 379,629-byte data exfiltration)

**Downloaded files (PE32 DLLs disguised as .jpg, delivered as HTTP POST responses)**

| Delivered as | SHA-256 | Type |
|---|---|---|
| 1.jpg | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` | PE32 DLL (console) |
| 2.jpg | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` | PE32 DLL (GUI) |
| 3.jpg | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` | PE32 DLL (GUI) |
| 4.jpg | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` | PE32 DLL (console) |
| 5.jpg | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` | PE32 DLL (GUI) |
| 6.jpg | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` | PE32 DLL (GUI) |
| 7.jpg | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` | PE32 DLL (console) |

**Exfiltrated file**
- `_5861695120.zip` (379,629 bytes), uploaded to `2.56.57.108` at 20:07:36 — contains stolen Chrome/Edge autofill, saved credit cards, cookies, saved passwords, Outlook data, a crypto-wallet-key folder (`pvk/`), a system-info file, and a desktop screenshot.

## Not observed / ruled out
- No Cobalt Strike, DarkVNC, or secondary C2 traffic in this pcap.
- No other internal hosts show malicious activity — the compromise is confined to 192.168.1.216.
- No IDS/Suricata alert file was present in the evidence directory to cross-check against.
